subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 2-year-old girl is brought for gait deterioration. She began walking at 14 months but now stumbles frequently, and her parents report slurred speech and declining interest in play. Examination shows ataxia, spasticity, hyperreflexia in the legs, and diminished vibration sense distally. MRI shows symmetric confluent demyelination of the cerebral white matter, and nerve conduction studies show slowed conduction. Urine sediment contains metachromatic granules.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is an autosomal recessive deficiency of arylsulfatase A that leads to accumulation of cerebroside sulfate (sulfatide). Sulfatide is toxic to myelin-forming cells, producing combined central and peripheral demyelination with ataxia, spasticity, and dementia. Metachromatic granules are seen in oligodendrocytes, macrophages, and urine sediment, which is the source of the disease name.

explanation_incorrect.A: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease, in which globoid cells and psychosine toxicity predominate.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease, which affects neurons rather than myelin and produces a cherry-red spot.
explanation_incorrect.D: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease, with hepatosplenomegaly, foam cells, and a cherry-red spot.
explanation_incorrect.E: α-L-Iduronidase deficiency causes Hurler syndrome, a mucopolysaccharidosis with coarse facies and skeletal dysplasia.

educationalObjective: Progressive central and peripheral demyelination with ataxia and metachromatic granules indicates metachromatic leukodystrophy due to arylsulfatase A deficiency.
